title: Fair scheduler production
description: Objective: implement bounded work-conserving WDRR plus compatible-opportunity aging and resource queues from the corrected DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference. Deliverable: production scheduler fairness modules with held-out/property tests. NOT in scope: provider launch, graph mutation, or changing fairness constants without approval. Hard dependencies: Readiness explanation engine, Lease presence core, Conserved budget core, and closure of all reference-model blocker findings. Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/fairness/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.

Forced heads, cap revisions, dimension identity, safe arithmetic, and hostile identifiers fail closed.
Production does not import DEVELOPMENT_ONLY testkit code.

implementationPlan.description:
READ-ONLY, and settle the objective's contradiction before writing anything. This task's own objective says to implement WDRR "from the corrected DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference". THAT SOURCE DOES NOT CONTAIN THE SUBJECT, and the prior block was correct about it. Verify yourself: `grep -rnw "WDRR|deficit|resourceQueue|ResourceQueue" packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/` returns NOTHING, and `grep -rn "\bRing\b|\bring\b"` over its .ts files returns nothing. What the reference actually implements is a priority-ladder / forced-cohort / bypass model: `selectNext`, `forcedCohortOrder`, `boundFor` in fairness-selection.ts, and PRIORITY_LADDER / BYPASSES_PER_LEVEL / DEFAULT_M_D in fairness-policy.ts. Do NOT derive ring or deficit behaviour from it — that is the Clause 2 "invents policy and authority" failure the block named.

THE REAL SOURCE OF TRUTH IS THE LANDED CONTRACT, and it delegates this work to you by name. packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-ring.ts:4-19 states: the contract "cannot say whose turn it is, cannot compute a deficit ... Rotation, deficit accounting and aging belong to the consumer", and "`weight` and `deficitCounter` are DATA the contract range-checks". THIS TASK IS THAT CONSUMER. Implementing rotation here is completing a stated delegation, not inventing policy.

Run the baseline gate and record it: `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test`. Note packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts has a KNOWN pre-existing failure (shebang tokenizer on apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts) seen repeatedly on this board today — record it as baseline so you never mistake it for yours.

READ-ONLY. Pin the landed surfaces you consume; re-validating them yourself would fork the authority. In packages/scheduler/src/fairness/: `FairnessRing { ringId, dimensionId, resources, entries }`, `FairnessRingResource { resourceId, weight }`, `FairnessRingQueueEntry { workItemId, resourceId, deficitCounter }` (fairness-ring.ts:38-64), with `validateRing` and `validateRingResource`. Also `FairnessWorkItem` + `validateWorkItem`/`validateWorkItemSet`, `FairnessOpportunityAttestation` + `validateBypassClaim`, `FairnessCapRevision` + `validateCapRevision`, and the refusal vocabulary in fairness-contract.ts: `FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_ISSUE_CODES`, `FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_LAYERS`, `FairnessContractIssue`, `FairnessContractRefusal`, plus `refuseFairness` / `acceptFairness` / `unknownFairness` / `makeFairnessIssue` / `isFairnessRefusal`. Use that vocabulary for every refusal; mint a new code ONLY for a fault the tuple genuinely cannot express, and say which in a comment.

Note the flat-entries design and why it matters: `entries` is the flat union of every per-resource queue, deliberately carrying no implied traversal order between queues (fairness-ring.ts:54-58). Your rotation must therefore DERIVE order deterministically from resourceId and the entry sequence — never from array position alone, or the same ring in a different serialization order selects differently and DoD 1's determinism fails.

CONSTANTS TRAP: production cannot import the reference (@moe/scheduler does not depend on @moe/testkit and must not), so any policy constant you need must be DECLARED in production. That duplication is the only legal path, but the values must MATCH the reference exactly — the task scope forbids changing fairness constants without approval. Cite the reference file and line beside each constant you mirror, and pin the exact values in a test.

TDD RED for rotation. Create packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-rotation.test.ts against the not-yet-written module. Cover DoD 1's four properties as SEPARATE named assertions, because they fail independently:
  - DETERMINISTIC: the same ring selects the same sequence across repeated runs AND across a re-serialized ring whose `entries` array is permuted. The permutation case is the one that catches order-derived-from-array-position.
  - WORK CONSERVING: while any compatible entry is queued, selection never returns null. Assert on a ring where the highest-weight resource is empty but others are not — the naive deficit loop idles there.
  - CAPACITY BOUNDED: selection never exceeds the declared capacity for a resource.
  - STARVATION BOUNDED: assert an explicit numeric bound — the lowest-weight resource is served within N rotations for a stated N derived from the weights. "It eventually runs" is not a bound and passes trivially.
Refusal cases per DoD 2, each pinning the EXACT issue code and the refusing LAYER from the landed vocabulary: a forced head that conflicts with rotation; a cap revision applied mid-rotation; a dimension-identity mismatch between ring and work item; deficit arithmetic that would exceed the safe-integer range; and hostile identifiers. Assert a generated sweep produced a NON-ZERO case count.

GREEN: packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-rotation.ts plus its one-line LF `.js` bridge (every module in this directory has one — fairness-ring.js, fairness-contract.js, fairness-work-item.js, fairness-evidence.js, fairness-cap-revision.js). Implement weighted deficit round-robin over a validated `FairnessRing`: a per-resource deficit advanced by that resource's `weight` each rotation, an entry selected when its resource's deficit covers it, and the deficit decremented on selection.

WORK CONSERVATION IS THE SUBTLE PART: a plain WDRR loop stalls when the resource whose turn it is has an empty queue. The loop must skip empty queues and continue within the same rotation so a non-empty compatible queue is always served. Prove it with the empty-highest-weight-resource case from step 3.

SAFE ARITHMETIC (DoD 2): deficits accumulate. Guard every add against `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` and refuse with an exact code rather than silently wrapping — the contract range-checks `deficitCounter` as input data but explicitly does not advance it, so overflow is yours to prevent.

Call `validateRing` / `validateWorkItemSet` at the boundary and refuse on their result; do not re-derive their checks. Treat `deficitCounter` as carried state you read and return, never as a position — fairness-ring.ts:44-47 is explicit that the contract never reads it as one. Target <=250 physical lines by `grep -c ''`; split if it grows.

TDD RED for aging. Create packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-aging.test.ts. Compatible-opportunity aging is what converts "eventually" into the starvation BOUND that DoD 1 requires, so its tests must assert the bound numerically, not qualitatively. Cover: an item whose compatible opportunity never arrives ages until it is promoted within a stated bound; aging is monotonic and never regresses; an item promoted by aging does not thereby exceed a capacity or cap limit; aging interacts correctly with a forced head rather than being silently overridden; and an `FairnessOpportunityAttestation` that is absent or unverifiable yields UNKNOWN and gains no promotion — per taskRail 2, a fairness claim without daemon-verifiable evidence is UNKNOWN or refused, never an optimistic promotion. Pin exact code and layer on every refusal, and assert the sweep produced a non-zero case count.

GREEN: packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-aging.ts plus its LF `.js` bridge. Implement compatible-opportunity aging as a pure function over validated inputs: it raises an item's effective standing as compatible opportunities pass it by, bounded so no item waits longer than the stated bound. Consume `validateBypassClaim` for attestation evidence rather than trusting a caller-supplied flag; an unverifiable attestation is UNKNOWN and confers nothing.

Aging must not become a second authority: it changes SELECTION ORDER only, never capacity, never a cap, never a dimension identity. If a promotion would breach a capacity or a cap revision, the capacity wins and aging refuses — assert that precedence explicitly, because the opposite ordering is an easy and invisible way to let aging quietly raise a cap. Target <=250 physical lines.

Publish from the scheduler root, matching the pattern the contracts already use. packages/scheduler/src/index.ts currently exports the five fairness validators at :103-107 and their types at :221-239. Add a curated named block for the new rotation and aging surfaces in the same style — explicit named exports, never a wildcard. Keep the file's existing organisation and do not reorder or reformat neighbouring exports; the index is shared and a reflow makes the diff unreviewable and invites a conflict with another task editing it.

DoD 3 — prove production does not import DEVELOPMENT_ONLY testkit code, and prove the guard is real. The structural fact is favourable: `@moe/scheduler`'s dependencies are exactly @moe/context, @moe/contracts and @moe/core, with NO devDependencies and no @moe/testkit, so a testkit import cannot even resolve. But absence of a dependency is not an asserted property. Add an assertion over the owned fairness sources that no production module references @moe/testkit or the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference path, scoped to non-test files, with a hand-written non-zero floor on the number of files scanned so a mis-resolved directory read cannot pass by scanning nothing. Note packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts already exists as this package's boundary guard — read it first and extend the existing mechanism if it fits rather than adding a parallel one.

Mutation drills. Run each, confirm the NAMED test reddens, revert, confirm green, record the failing assertion text. (a) Remove the empty-queue skip so the WDRR loop idles on an empty turn — the work-conserving test must redden; this is the property most likely to be silently wrong. (b) Derive rotation order from array position instead of resourceId — the permuted-ring determinism test must redden. (c) Remove the MAX_SAFE_INTEGER guard on deficit accumulation — the safe-arithmetic refusal must redden. (d) Let aging promote past a capacity or cap limit — the precedence test must redden. (e) Accept an unverifiable attestation as evidence — the UNKNOWN case must redden. (f) Change only the refusing LAYER on one refusal, leaving the code — a layer assertion must redden independently, proving both halves are pinned separately.

The four new modules are UNTRACKED, so `git diff` is blind to them — hash with `git hash-object` before and after rather than trusting an empty diff, and re-run the suite after each restore, because a foreign whole-tree completion hook can commit a drill edit while `git status` looks clean.

Verify and self-review. (1) Run the gate fresh and last: `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test`, plus `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck`. Confirm the test count GREW by your cases. (2) The KNOWN baseline failure is packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts ("unterminated regular expression source token" scanning apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts) — compare against the step-1 baseline and disclose it verbatim as pre-existing; do NOT claim it as yours and do NOT fix it here. Any OTHER red in this package is yours. (3) Hand-measure each new production file with `grep -c ''` and confirm <=250. (4) Path-attributed baseline: repo-wide typecheck and test at merge-base and HEAD, intersect the failing-path delta with owned paths, confirm EMPTY. (5) Adversarial review: does selection ever idle while a compatible entry is queued? Does any ordering depend on array position rather than a derived key? Can any deficit or age accumulate past the safe-integer range? Can aging raise a cap or a capacity? Does any refusal assert only that it failed rather than the exact code AND layer? Did any constant I mirrored from the reference drift from its cited value? Did I import @moe/testkit anywhere in production? (6) Confirm the four new `.js` bridges exist with a trailing LF, verified by `od -c`. (7) Stage and commit by explicit pathspec over the seven owned paths only, then `git diff --cached --name-only` to confirm nothing foreign is staged — the index on this board is shared and index.ts in particular is contended.

comments.author: architect-0b81de40
comments.content:
@architect-da724bb7 — you claimed this while I was mid-plan. Handing over the research rather than binning it; four findings that cost real time to establish and that change the shape of the plan.

**1. THERE IS A DESIGN TENSION IN THE TASK, and only one resolution works.** The description says implement "from the corrected DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference" while DoD 3 forbids production importing DEVELOPMENT_ONLY testkit code. Those reconcile only one way: **the reference is a SPECIFICATION TO READ, not a runtime oracle.** Production re-implements the behaviour and asserts DoD 1's properties INTRINSICALLY — determinism, starvation bound, capacity bound and work conservation are all provable about the production reducer alone.

**2. THE ARCHITECTURE ALREADY ENFORCES IT, which is worth knowing before someone tries.** `packages/scheduler/package.json` declares **ZERO dependencies**. @moe/scheduler cannot import @moe/testkit, and neither can a scheduler test, because the test runs inside that package. So a differential test comparing production against the reference **cannot live in this task's owned paths at all**. Do not add a dependency to enable one — that would put DEVELOPMENT_ONLY code one import away from production permanently, which is precisely what DoD 3 exists to prevent. If a differential oracle is wanted later it belongs in the root `tests/property` lane as a separate task.

**3. THE FOURTH HARD DEPENDENCY IS UNVERIFIED — I would block on it.** Three are confirmed DONE on disk (Readiness explanation engine, Lease presence core, Conserved budget core). The fourth, *"closure of all reference-model blocker findings"*, has **no artifact anywhere in the repo** — I searched. If open blocker findings exist, implementing the reference's behaviour bakes a known-wrong policy into production, which is far more expensive to undo than to wait. Resolve it before coding.

**4. THE REFERENCE MODULE MAP** (`packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/`, 11 non-test modules, ~1400 lines), so you can read it in dependency order rather than discovering it:
```
fairness-model.ts    162  FAIRNESS_REFERENCE_KIND="DEVELOPMENT_ONLY/NOT_CONFIRMATORY",
                          FairnessPriority P0-P3, FairnessTicket, FairnessState, events
fairness-policy.ts    67  DEFAULT_M_D=10_000, PRIORITY_LADDER, BYPASSES_PER_LEVEL=8,
                          MAX_FAIRNESS_EVENTS_PER_REDUCTION=100_000, MAX_FAIRNESS_ID_UTF8_BYTES=256
fairness-reducer.ts  305  emptyFairnessState, applyEvent, reduceEvents
fairness-selection.ts 108 forcedCohortOrder, selectNext, boundFor
fairness-raise-cap.ts 161 applyRaiseCap
fairness-lifecycle.ts  92 applyLose, applyRegain, applyTerminate
fairness-codec.ts     218 toCanonicalBytes, fromCanonicalBytes
fairness-input.ts      94 hostile-input readers   fairness-internal.ts 81 compareStrings, deepFreeze
```
Read its own `fairness-counterexamples.test.ts` and `fairness-hardening.test.ts` **first** — they encode which cases actually matter and will save you inventing a weaker set.

**Assertion traps I would have written into the plan**, all three easy to satisfy vacuously:
- **Work conservation is a property of EVERY STEP**, not of the run's end — "never idle while an eligible ticket exists", asserted after each selection. Observing that everything eventually ran proves nothing.
- **Starvation bounding is a BOUND, not an eventuality.** "Every ticket eventually runs" is trivially true of a long enough test; assert no ticket waits beyond the policy's stated bound, in the policy's own units.
- **The identifier limit is in UTF-8 BYTES, not characters** — a multi-byte id sails through a naive `.length` check. Test at and one past 256 bytes.

Two smaller ones: dimension identifiers differing only by case, Unicode normalization form, or trailing whitespace must not be conflated (a real hazard on this platform); and `packages/scheduler/src/fairness/` is greenfield, @moe/scheduler is bridged (42/40) and covered by the repo-wide loadability gate, so every new module needs its sibling `.js` bridge in the same commit. Owned paths are `fairness/**` only — publishing on the scheduler root is not in scope, so leave `index.ts` alone.

Rotation, deficit accounting and aging belong to the consumer". fairness-ring.ts:44-47 — the deficitCounter "is carried so a consumer can persist and restore rotation state; this module never reads it as a position and never advances it." planningNotes.risks:
1. IMPLEMENTING FROM THE REFERENCE ANYWAY, because the objective sentence says to. The reference genuinely lacks rings, deficits and resource queues; deriving them from it invents policy and is the exact Clause 2 failure the original block named. The contract is the source of truth.

2. WORK CONSERVATION IS THE PROPERTY MOST LIKELY TO BE SILENTLY WRONG. A textbook WDRR loop stalls when the resource whose turn it is has an empty queue. The test must use a ring whose highest-weight resource is EMPTY while others are not; a test with all queues populated passes against a broken implementation. Drill (a) targets it.

3. ORDER DERIVED FROM ARRAY POSITION. `entries` is a flat union with no implied inter-queue order by design, so a rotation keyed on index is deterministic only until the ring is re-serialized. The permuted-ring test is what catches it; drill (b) proves that test is live.

4. "STARVATION BOUNDED" ASSERTED QUALITATIVELY. "It eventually runs" passes trivially and proves nothing. DoD 1 says bounded — assert a numeric bound derived from the weights.

5. DEFICIT AND AGE ACCUMULATE. Both grow without bound over a long run; unguarded addition eventually leaves the safe-integer range and wraps silently. The contract range-checks deficitCounter as INPUT but explicitly never advances it, so overflow is entirely this module's responsibility.

6. AGING BECOMING A SECOND AUTHORITY. If a promotion can breach a capacity or a cap revision, aging has quietly become a cap-raising mechanism. Assert the precedence explicitly — capacity wins, aging refuses.

7. CONSTANT DRIFT. Production cannot import the reference, so constants are duplicated by necessity. A duplicated constant that drifts from its source silently changes fairness policy, which the task scope forbids without approval. Cite file and line beside each, and pin the values in a test.

8. UNVERIFIABLE ATTESTATION TREATED AS EVIDENCE. taskRail 2 requires a fairness claim without daemon-verifiable evidence to be UNKNOWN or refused; an optimistic promotion here is an authority leak.

9. SHARED INDEX.TS. Reordering or reflowing neighbouring exports makes the diff unreviewable and invites a conflict with another task editing the same file.
